newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY-FREE STATE TRAVEL TO THE BULLRING.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY-FREE STATE TRAVEL TO THE BULLRING.

text.p: The most revealing fixture of the latest round of the Currie Cup will be at Loftus Versfeld in Pretoria where Free State take on Northern Transvaal on Saturday.
The suspicion that Northerns peaked for the Super 12 and have not yet managed to rebuild their desire will be tested to the full by Helgard Muller's team.
The most important game in group A is in Witbank where Boland will attempt to overturn South Eastern Transvaal in the race for the last quarter final slot in their section.
New Springbok forward coach Nick Mallett has done wonders with the limited talent at his disposal among the winefarmers, but he will be under no illiusions about the difficulty of winning in Witbank.

South Easts were desperately unlucky to lose to Transvaal at Ellis Park last week and were full value for a a draw against the 1993/4 champions earlier in the season. Their powerful pack should prove too much for the visitors, but a red blooded encounter is assured.
Transvaal will travel to Port Elizabeth with less confidence than they would have wished after their dismal display last week, but against struggling EP they should come back with the points.

The return of Hennie le Roux to flyhalf should ensure a more fluent game plan among the backs, while all eyes will be on the fit again Balie Swart who will be trying to re-establish his claim for the Springbok tighthead berth.

In other games Griqualand West should have no problems against Northern Free State in Kimberley on Friday night while the match ups between South Westen Districts and Eastern Transvaal and Western Transvaal and Border will be of little more than academic interest.
